items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: Some little lieutenant in Remes, France. I get in and this guy had just come from America... So I'd put on you know, Sergeant Plotsky or it didn't make any difference what the name was.

ctx.x: Some little lieutenant in Remes, France. I get in and this guy had just come from America and hadn't seen any action or anything. A young guy and a smart alec and he was selling money orders to me, a lieutenant!. An officer, selling me money orders. He wanted to sell me money orders. Three hundred francs for one hundred dollars, in other words, three to one.

And by that time we had currency control books. Now whatever my salary was why that was the amount of money I could send home by American Express I mean, postal money orders I should say. And the same thing with anyone. Your currency control books, they call it.
